question: Should OpenClaw sponsor official FreeBSD support, and if so should it be community/experimental support or Tier 1 release support?
rationale: The codebase can partially run on Node platforms and a community port exists, but official FreeBSD support would change the product support contract across packaging, docs, service lifecycle, and release validation.

options.title: Define Community FreeBSD Scope
options.body: Recognize the external ports/pkg path as community or experimental until owners, docs, service behavior, upgrade tracking, and release smoke expectations are named.

options.title: Promote Toward Tier 1
options.body: Accept ongoing FreeBSD release ownership and open tracked implementation work for pkg/ports coordination, service management, CI, docs, and validation.

options.title: Decline Official Support
options.body: Leave FreeBSD as external/community packaging and close the support-tier request after documenting that policy.

recommendation.title: Define Community FreeBSD Scope
recommendation.body: Recognize the external ports/pkg path as community or experimental until owners, docs, service behavior, upgrade tracking, and release smoke expectations are named.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses official support scope, release validation, installer publication, and roadmap ownership.
